suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-17 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited primary-care study found that clinically significant somatization syndrome overlaps extensively with depressive and anxiety syndromes, with more than half of cases showing comorbidity among the three syndromes. Require independently established DSM-5 somatic symptom disorder and separately established depressive disorder; the cited primary-care study reports syndromal overlap between somatization, depression, and anxiety and does not establish onset order or direction. Preserve medically explained symptoms, other psychiatric illness, substance use, medications, and shared vulnerability as competing explanations. Do not infer a depressive disorder from somatic symptoms, health concerns, or functional impairment alone, and do not treat this population-level association as proof that somatic symptom disorder caused an individual's depressive disorder. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
